summary.text: Sumer is the earliest known civilization, in southern Mesopotamia in what is now south-central Iraq.
Sumerian farmers along the Tigris and Euphrates grew a surplus of grain and other crops, which enabled them to form urban settlements.
The world's earliest known texts come from the Sumerian cities of Uruk and Jemdet Nasr.

facts.label: Their name for the land
facts.value: Kengir, the country of the noble lords

facts.label: City-state rulers
facts.value: A priestly governor (ensi) or a king (lugal)

facts.label: Earliest texts
facts.value: From Uruk and Jemdet Nasr, c. 3350 to 2500 BC

items.prompt: Sumerian farmers along the rivers grew more grain and crops than they needed. What did that extra allow?

options.label: A switch to hunting and fishing
The formation of urban settlements
A move to the Persian Gulf coast
The invention of the Akkadian language

items.explain: The surplus of grain and other crops enabled the farmers to form urban settlements.

items.prompt: A visitor to a Sumerian city-state in the late 4th millennium BC would find its life organised around what?

options.label: A grain market run by merchants
A royal army camp on the border
A canal junction run by farmers
A temple to the city's patron deity

items.explain: Each city-state was centered on a temple dedicated to its patron god or goddess, and its ruler was tied to the city's religious rites.

items.prompt: The name 'Sumer' that historians use was not the Sumerians' own word for their land. Whose word was it?

options.label: The Akkadians, who later conquered the cities
The Greeks, who wrote about the region
The Ubaidians, who lived there before them
The Sumerians, in their own inscriptions

items.explain: The Akkadians gave Sumer its main historical name; the Sumerians called their land Kengir.

items.prompt: Semitic-speaking kings of Akkad conquered Sumer. What role did the Sumerian language keep afterwards?

options.label: The language of the conquerors' army
The official tongue of far-off Egypt
A language kept for sacred use
A script reserved for private letters

items.explain: Sumerian continued as a sacred language even after the Akkadian conquest.

items.prompt: Before the Sumerians, a prehistoric people is assumed to have drained marshes for farming, developed trade and set up weaving and pottery. Who were they?

options.label: The Akkadians, from the northwest
The Ubaidians, a prehistoric people
The Natufians, early hunter-gatherers
The Dilmun islanders from Bahrain

items.explain: Modern scholars assume the Ubaidians were the first civilizing force in Sumer, though the Sumerians never mention them.

items.prompt: Sumer is counted as one of the cradles of civilization. Which of these is named alongside it?

options.label: The Indus Valley
The Roman Republic
Classical Athens
The Mongol Empire

items.explain: Sumer is listed with Egypt, the Indus Valley, the Erligang culture, Caral-Supe and Mesoamerica.
